messages:
support_alex: FYI NimbusRetail hitting us with bunch of 429s and user-reported latency spikes on their Dedicated pool since ~09:15 UTC. Customer says it started after a batch job window.

jules (oncall): looking now — can you paste an example request id or tenant id?

support_alex: tenant=nimbus-retail-42, request ids: req_01F8Y..., req_01F90... ; customer attached a short trace showing multiple 429s then one huge tail-latency.

amina (eng-sre): pulling metrics from dedicated pool for tenant. I see repeated scale-up -> scale-down cycles starting at 09:12. CPU spikes to ~82% then drops under threshold within ~30s -> autoscaler removes nodes -> repeat. Sounds like a classic stair-step.

runtime_lead: that pattern will produce 429s if we shrink faster than KV cache warm-up or if small bursts drive transient CPU. What's current cooldown?

amina (eng-sre): cooldown configured 60s, scale threshold: cpu > 70% for 2 samples (30s scrape). smoothing window: none.

ops_maya: also seeing intermittent NVMe throttling on those GPUs around same times (io.wait spikes). Could be noisy tenant doing big checkpointing or backup job during batch window.

jules (oncall): reproduction attempt: spinning a background job on another tenant in the same dedicated pool that reads ~500MB/s for 1m — eager to see if it triggers the same oscillation. Will run against staging.

amina (eng-sre): quick grep of logs shows evictions for pod nimbus-serve-0 at scale-down events. KV cache gets cleared on eviction which increases CPU on next warm-up -> vicious cycle.

mel (pm): Customer is asking for immediate mitigation — they want consistent throughput. Any short-term config we can flip?

runtime_lead: immediate mitigations: 1) increase scale-down cooldown to 300s, 2) enable metric smoothing (5m EMA) for autoscaler, 3) mark NimbusRetail tenants with stronger isolation policy (pin to dedicated subset) if available. 4) temporary max-downscale to avoid removing more than 1 replica per minute.

jules (oncall): agree. I'll patch autoscale config for that pool and monitor.

infra_bot: deploy request queued: patch autoscaler config for pool=dedicated-eu-west-2-nimbus, change: scaleDownCooldown=300s, smoothing=5m-EMA, maxDownPerMinute=1. PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/ops/patch/3456

deploy-bot: canary rollout scheduled to 3 hosts at 09:42 UTC. Rollback policy: automatic on 5% error increase in 10m window.

amina (eng-sre): added an alert for rapid scale churn (>=3 scale events in 6m) and leakage of KV cache evictions. Also flagged the tenant's background job traces to Customer Success to ask them to reschedule window.

support_alex: told customer we applied a mitigation and to expect lower 429s in ~10-15m. They asked whether billing spikes are possible because of repeated scale-ups — any ETA on cost impact?

runtime_lead: short-term cost bump possible while cooldown is larger since we won't scale down as aggressively. But cheaper than production outages. We'll quantify after next hour of telemetry.

ops_maya: for root-cause, we should repro locally: steps I used in staging: 1) start a continuous KV read job on tenant-bkg-1: curl -X POST https://staging-load/kv-read -d '{"rate_mb_s":500,"duration_s":60}' 2) run steady generation load on target tenant at ~200rps. That yields same stair-step within 2 cycles.

jules (oncall): noting commands to collect debug:

```
# capture timeline
kubectl -n rwd logs -l app=autoscaler --since=20m > /tmp/autoscaler.log
kubectl -n rwd get pods -o wide --selector=tenant=nimbus-retail-42 > /tmp/pods.txt
promql: rate(cpu_usage_seconds_total[30s]) by (pod)
promql: increase(kv_cache_evictions_total[10m])
```

runtime_lead: long-term fixes: 1) better metric smoothing (use 5m MA or scaled percentiles), 2) prefer vertical buffer (reserve one warm replica) for noisy pools, 3) tenant isolation / migration tooling, 4) detect heavy disk/io jobs and preemptively throttle or offload them to maintenance window.

mel (pm): can you add a short-run playbook for support to use when a customer reports this pattern? Also include cost guidance.

amina (eng-sre): will draft a 1-pager. For now, I'll keep monitoring. Current dashboard shows canary healthy at 09:48 — errors down from 12% -> 1.4%.

support_alex: customer confirmed drop in 429s and less burst latency. Thanks team.

jules (oncall): leaving note for postmortem if we still see recurrence after 24h. For now, closing escalation after telemetry stable for 2h.

infra_bot: ticket updated: ESC-2026 set to status=mitigated by jules.

runtime_lead: follow-up actions assigned: amina (draft playbook), infra (investigate NVMe throttling), ops (repro harness + load job throttling), pm (customer comms recap).

ops_maya: one more note — if we enable maxDownPerMinute we should watch for accidental long-term waste; suggest adding automated cost-signal to revert if sustained idle > 30m.

jules (oncall): good call. I'll add that to the playbook. Closing thread if no more alerts in 2h. :thumbsup:
